article_title: A New Item Response Theory Model for Open-Ended Online Homework with Multiple Allowed Attempts
citation: Emre Gönülateş and Gerd Kortemeyer. (2015). A New Item Response Theory Model for Open-Ended Online Homework with Multiple Allowed Attempts. https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06287
title: The 2P3TL model: a two-parameter three-trait logistic IRT model for open-ended online homework
description: The 2P3TL model extends the standard two-parameter logistic IRT model by introducing two learner traits beyond ability: a copying trait χj, which lifts the lower limit of the item characteristic curve so that even low-ability students can appear to solve problems, and a guessing trait γj, which lowers the probability that even high-ability students answer correctly. The article states that "The copying trait χj allows even low-ability students to "solve" problems, as it lifts the lower limit of the item characteristic curve." The guessing trait models random guessing, i.e., inputting answers without truly figuring out the solution, and is explicitly distinguished from the item-level guessing parameter ci of 3PL models.
requirements: Requires first-attempt data from open-ended online homework where guessing and copying behaviors occur
Parameter estimation via a simplified Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm
constraints: The guessing trait is meant to model random guessing in spite of knowing better, not last-minute guessing due to inability, which should continue to be modeled by ability
Parameters were constrained to a range of negative to positive ten for stability; reaching those limits is considered divergent
target_learners: University physics students in large-enrollment courses
target_learning_goals: Accurate assessment of learner ability from formative online homework data
examples: Applied to first-attempt data from 13 online homework assignments with 401 problems in a 256-student physics course
key_sources: Emre Gönülateş and Gerd Kortemeyer. (2015). A New Item Response Theory Model for Open-Ended Online Homework with Multiple Allowed Attempts. https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06287

article_title: Quantitatively ranking incorrect responses to multiple-choice questions using item response theory
citation: Trevor I. Smith, Kyle J. Louis, Bartholomew J. Ricci, IV, and Nasrine Bendjilali. (2019). Quantitatively ranking incorrect responses to multiple-choice questions using item response theory. https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00521
title: 2PL-NRM nested logit item response theory model for ranking incorrect responses
description: The model combines the two-parameter logistic IRT model, which estimates each student's latent trait theta and each question's difficulty and discrimination, with Bock's nominal response model applied to the incorrect responses only. The ak parameter of each incorrect response measures its correlation with the latent trait, so "a higher value indicating a response that is more closely correlated with the latent trait and, therefore, better". The authors use the mirt package in R and rank responses by comparing ak distributions generated by repeated random sampling.
requirements: A data set with at least 10 times as many response sets as parameters to be calculated, per de Ayala as cited in the article
A dummy response set with a0 = 0 to uniquely determine each ak parameter
constraints: ak values are only meaningful when compared within the same question
Response J is omitted because it does not represent a well-defined indication of what each student would consider correct
The third guessing parameter of the 3PL model was judged inappropriate because FMCE responses are concentrated in a small subset of choices
target_learning_goals: Newtonian mechanics conceptual understanding as measured by the FMCE
key_sources: Trevor I. Smith, Kyle J. Louis, Bartholomew J. Ricci, IV, and Nasrine Bendjilali. (2019). Quantitatively ranking incorrect responses to multiple-choice questions using item response theory. https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00521
